text: I have never felt such pity for any one in this wide world as I felt for that half-witted creature, and it began to come over me that the brig Covenant (for all her pious name) was little better than a hell upon the seas. “Have you no friends?” said I. He said he had a father in some English seaport, I forget which. “He was a fine man, too,” he said, “but he’s dead.” “In Heaven’s name,” cried I, “can you find no reputable life on shore?” “O, no,” says he, winking and looking very sly, “they would put me to a trade. I know a trick worth two of that, I do!” I asked him what trade could be so dreadful as the one he followed, where he ran the continual peril of his life, not alone from wind and sea, but by the horrid cruelty of those who were his masters.
